section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the psalm and the Midrashic interpretation that it speaks of the future redemption, contrasting the masculine and feminine forms of song.
section.t: "Halleluyah! Sing to God a new song, His praise in the congregation of chassidim,"
and it concludes,
"The exaltations of God are in their throat, and a double-edged sword is in their hand."
For in the verses after this, it explains what they will do with the sword, etc.
Now, it is brought in the Midrash Tehillim in its place that this psalm speaks about the future: Who are the chassidim? These are Israel.
Whenever they see the Holy One, blessed be He, they become chassidim, etc.
They saw Him at the sea, they became chassidim and said a song, as it is stated,
"Then Moshe sang," etc.
And when they see Him in the World to Come, they become chassidim, as it is stated, "His praise in the congregation of chassidim."
And so it is brought in the Mechilta and Yalkut on Parshat Beshalach that this song is for the future to come.
Therefore it says "a new song" in the masculine form,
while in many places it is stated "a new song" in the feminine form.
And even regarding the redemption from Egypt, it says "this song" in the feminine form.
And as it is explained in Shir HaShirim Rabbah
(on the verse "I am black but comely"):

A female takes a tenth of the property, etc. So Israel inherited the land of the seven nations, which is a tenth of the seventy nations, etc., they said a song in the feminine form, etc., as it is stated, "this song to God,"
But in the future, they are destined to inherit like a male who inherits all of his father's property, etc., they will say it in the masculine form.
And we need to understand the statement, "The exaltations of God are in their throat, and a double-edged sword is in their hand,"
for since it speaks of the future redemption,
then what is the matter of the sword?
For in the future it is written,
"And they shall beat their swords into plowshares... nation shall not lift up sword against nation."
